epithet: The ant, the hoopoe and the queen
lede: A king who understood the speech of birds, an ant that warned her colony, a bird that brought news of a throne — and a queen who came to see for herself and said, “I submit, with Sulaymān, to Allah.” It is the one surah with the basmalah written inside it.

names.name: al-Naml
names.note: After the valley of the ants in its eighteenth ayah. It is also called Sūrat Sulaymān, and Ṭā Sīn, after the two letters it opens with.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all: Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī both record the agreement. It is the middle one of three surahs that open with the letters Ṭā Sīn and came down in the order in which they stand: al-Shuʿarāʾ, al-Naml, al-Qaṣaṣ. The traditional order places it forty-eighth.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ النَّمْلِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّهَا فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ، وَهِيَ ثَلَاثٌ وتسعون آية

setting: No occasion is reported for it. Its opening lines say whom it is for — “guidance and good news for the believers” — and whom it is not for: “those who do not believe in the Hereafter: We have made their deeds seem fair to them, so they wander blindly.”

The surah that follows is about knowledge, and what people do with it. Mūsā is shown nine signs, and Pharaoh’s people reject them “though their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and pride.” Then come Dāwūd and Sulaymān, who were given knowledge and said, “Praise be to Allah, who has favoured us above many of His believing servants.” That is the contrast the whole surah turns on. The men of Quraysh were not short of evidence. They were short of gratitude.

The story of Sulaymān is told here more fully than anywhere else. His hosts of jinn, men and birds march in ranks; an ant tells her kind to go indoors lest they be trampled unawares, and he smiles at her words and thanks his Lord. The hoopoe is missing from the muster and comes back with a report: a woman ruling a people, with a mighty throne, and they bow to the sun. The letter he sends her begins: “In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.” She consults her council, tests him with a gift, and at last comes herself — to find her own throne there before her, and a floor of glass she takes for water. Her words on seeing it are the point of the story: “My Lord, I have wronged myself; and I submit, with Sulaymān, to Allah, Lord of the worlds.” A sovereign with every worldly reason for pride did what the chiefs of Makkah would not.

Then the surah puts five questions to its hearers, each ending, “Is there a god with Allah?” — who created the heavens and the earth; who made the earth firm; who answers the one in distress when he calls; who guides you through the darkness of land and sea; who begins creation and then repeats it.
aim: To recall Allah’s favour to the Prophet ﷺ in the greatest sign — the Qurʾan — and to urge thankfulness for it and patience in conveying it.

outline.title: The Qurʾan, and who receives it
outline.summary: Ṭā Sīn. These are the ayat of the Qurʾan and a clear Book: guidance and good news for the believers, who keep up the prayer, give the zakāh, and are certain of the Hereafter. You are receiving the Qurʾan from One who is Wise, All-Knowing.

outline.title: Mūsā at the fire
outline.summary: Mūsā said to his family, “I perceive a fire.” When he came to it he was called: “Blessed is whoever is at the fire and whoever is around it. Mūsā, it is I, Allah, the Almighty, the Wise. Throw down your staff.” Nine signs for Pharaoh and his people. They rejected them, though their own souls were convinced, out of injustice and pride.

outline.title: Sulaymān and the Queen of Sabaʾ
outline.summary: We gave knowledge to Dāwūd and Sulaymān. Sulaymān’s hosts were mustered; an ant said, “Enter your dwellings, lest Sulaymān and his hosts crush you unawares,” and he smiled. The hoopoe brought news from Sabaʾ of a queen and a people who prostrate to the sun. He wrote to her; she sent a gift; he sent it back. One with knowledge of the Book brought her throne before his glance returned to him: “This is of the bounty of my Lord, to test me — will I give thanks, or be ungrateful?” She came, and said: “I submit, with Sulaymān, to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”

outline.title: Ṣāliḥ, and Lūṭ
outline.summary: To Thamūd We sent their brother Ṣāliḥ, and they became two quarrelling factions. Nine men in the city swore to attack him and his family by night. They plotted, and We planned; there are their houses, fallen in. And Lūṭ, whose people said: “Expel the family of Lūṭ from your town; they are people who keep themselves pure.”

outline.title: Is there a god with Allah?
outline.summary: Say: praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen. Who created the heavens and the earth and sent down water for you? Who made the earth a fixed abode? Who answers the distressed one when he calls on Him, and removes the harm? Who guides you in the darkness of land and sea? Who originates creation and then repeats it? Is there a god with Allah? Say: none in the heavens or the earth knows the unseen but Allah.

outline.title: The deniers, and the Beast
outline.summary: Those who disbelieve say: “When we are dust, we and our fathers, shall we be brought out?” Travel through the land, and see how the guilty ended. Do not grieve over them. This Qurʾan relates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ. You cannot make the dead hear. And when the word falls upon them, We shall bring out for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them.

outline.title: The Day
outline.summary: The Day We gather from every nation a troop of those who denied Our signs. The Day the Trumpet is blown, and all in the heavens and the earth are terrified. You see the mountains and think them fixed, while they pass as the clouds pass. Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it. Say: I am commanded only to worship the Lord of this city, who made it sacred. And say: praise be to Allah; He will show you His signs, and you will know them.

keyAyah.why: The third of the five questions, and the one every person has asked in his own life: who answers the one in distress?

virtues.text: “An ant bit one of the prophets, and he ordered the ant colony to be burned. Then Allah revealed to him: because a single ant bit you, you have burned a nation of those that glorify Allah?”

before: Al-Shuʿarāʾ told the stories of seven prophets, each ending in the destruction of those who denied. Al-Naml tells of prophets who were given power and knowledge — and of a ruler who believed.
after: Al-Naml gave a single scene from the life of Mūsā. Al-Qaṣaṣ goes back to his birth and tells the whole.
